stemMarkdown: A can do a job in 14 days. B is 60% more efficient than A. How many days does B take to do the same job alone? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Being 60% more efficient means B works at $160\%$ of A's rate, so B takes $\dfrac{100}{160}$ of A's time: $14 \times \dfrac{100}{160} = 8.75$ days.
altSolutionMarkdown: Efficiency and time are inversely related — more efficient means proportionally fewer days.
